name: How do plumbers locate underground drains?

mainEntity.name: How do plumbers locate underground drains?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plumbers typically locate underground drains using a combination of methods. The primary tool is a sewer camera equipped with a traceable sonde (transmitter). This camera is inserted into the drain line, and as it travels, the sonde emits a signal. A receiver held above ground detects this signal, allowing the technician to accurately map the pipe's exact location, depth, and direction. This non-invasive method provides precise data, helping to identify blockages, collapses, or bellies in the line without digging.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plumbers locate drains by inserting a sewer camera with a traceable sonde into the pipe. A receiver detects the sonde's signal above ground, mapping the drain's exact location and depth.
